title: Assessing pseudobulk DE adequacy with seny
text: assessAll() chains layers — pseudobulk setup, design/confounding (layer 1), pseudobulk quality (layer 2), variance structure sensitivity (layer 4) — returns one row per comparison. comparison table carries layer-2 cell-quality metrics alongside call. cells_cond_cor correlation log cells-per-sample condition; cells_ratio smaller group median larger; expected_recall share true effects target size test expected detect (mean per-gene power target), drives Adequate / Underpowered call. non-adequate call explains : CD4 T clean (Adequate); CD8 T far fewer cells condition B, cell-count imbalance tracks condition breaks equal-variance assumption (Caution — consider voom sampleWeights dreamlet precision weights); NK high -donor variance modest cell count, genes detectable target effect (Underpowered).
code: res <- assessAll(sce, sample = "donor", group = "condition",                  annotations = "cell_type", targetLFC = 1) #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes #> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes cols <- c("cluster", "nA", "nB", "median_cells", "gini_cells", "cells_ratio",           "cells_cond_cor", "n_testable", "expected_recall", "call") knitr::kable(as.data.frame(res)[, cols], digits = 2, row.names = FALSE) d <- as.data.frame(res) for (i in seq_len(nrow(d))) {     cat(d$cluster[i], "->", as.character(d$call[i]), "::", d$reason[i], "\n") } #> CD4T -> Adequate :: adequate  #> CD8T -> Caution :: cell-count imbalance correlated with condition (r -1.00, cutoff 0.50 at 24 samples; consider sample weights)  #> NK -> Adequate :: adequate

text: named list: cramerV (condition-covariate association comparison flagged Caution), vif (variance inflation factor threshold), sensitivity (expected recall target effect comparison adequately powered; 0.5 matches replication failure defined recall 0.5), minSamples (fewer samples per group Invalid), cellsCondCor (absolute correlation log cells per sample condition cell-count imbalance flagged Caution), cellsCondAlpha (correlation must also exceed critical value level comparison's sample size, chance correlations small designs flagged: cutoff max(cellsCondCor, r_crit(n)), 0.81 6 samples cellsCondCor ~16 samples), minTestable (fewer testable genes Underpowered). layer-2 values, like others, provisional placeholders E1-E8.

what: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity
title: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity
text: variance fits (estimateVariance()), computes analytic standard error two-group log2 fold-change contrast per gene (SE^2 = 1/sum_A w + 1/sum_B w, w = 1/(1/mu + phi), phi dispersion condition design), minimum detectable effect target power FDR, power primary target effect. Summarises comparison's expected recall targetLFC: mean per-gene power target testable genes, .e. share true effects size test expected detect spread like testable genes. callComparisons() calls comparison Adequate expected recall reaches defaultThresholds()$sensitivity (0.5). OneK1K known injected effects tracked observed recall per comparison (slope 1.0), whereas sensitivity fraction (share genes whose MDE clears target target power, still reported) -predicts (E4c). Uncalibrated MVP (calibrate = FALSE).

title: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity

title: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity
text: variance list returned estimateVariance(). targetLFC Primary target absolute log2 fold-change call. Default 1. power Target power. Default 0.8. fdr Target FDR. Default 0.05. pi1 Fraction true positives maps FDR per-gene threshold: "discoveries" (default) estimates per comparison fraction genes comparison's DE test calls fdr; number fixes every comparison (falls back 0.05 comparison whose fit p-values). alphaFixed Optional fixed per-gene significance level. NULL (default) uses pi1-mapped level alone; number makes call use stricter two (larger MDE). calibrate Reserved; must FALSE MVP.

title: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity
text: data.frame, one row per comparison, target_lfc, pi1 per-gene alpha used, expected_recall (summary behind call), sensitivity_fraction, median_mde, median_mde_fdr, median_mde_fixed (NA without alphaFixed) median_power.

title: Layer 4 (sensitivity): minimum detectable effect and power — estimateSensitivity
text: FDR target mapped per-gene significance level fraction true positives pi1 (Jung 2005), capped fdr (BH never tests gene FDR level). BH's realised per-gene threshold scales fraction genes calls, fixed pi1 suits every contrast: sparse contrast (male vs female blood, realised threshold ~1e-4) makes fixed 5% optimistic, dense one makes conservative. default (pi1 = "discoveries") comparison uses fraction BH discoveries, R / m DE test chosen method fdr (floored 1 / m), power evaluated threshold BH actually uses . OneK1K 0.5-20\ genes injected DE male vs female best calibrated rules tested (E4b).

what: Layer 4 (variance): null-model dispersion, decomposition and per-gene SE — estimateVariance
title: Layer 4 (variance): null-model dispersion, decomposition and per-gene SE — estimateVariance
text: every comparison, fits chosen DE method returns per-gene standard error two-group log2 fold-change contrast (used estimateSensitivity()). SE uses dispersion estimated condition design, user's test sees , evaluated condition-blind (null-model) fitted means. Power always computed target effect, never observed one. null-model dispersion absorb real effects noise understate power exactly DE strong. variance decomposition stays condition-blind. count methods (edgeR, deseq2) also splits pseudobulk negative-binomial dispersion phi_total cell-heterogeneity term (theta/n, cell-level theta pbSetup()) -donor term phi_donor (moment estimate max(0, phi_total - theta*mean(1/n))), reports depth/cell/donor variance shares regime label. voom method uses limma's precision-weight variance model, NB decomposition (columns NA).
